summary: Lerendor holds two crowns together, tolls the strait, leads the Leren Compact and the Long Watch, and answers the Question of the Strait: honour the treaty, stand apart, or seize the strait.

strait_merchants.name: Merchants of the Strait
strait_merchants.desc: Guilds of both shores trade freely under the king's seal and pay their dues without much argument.

toll_houses_spirit.name: Toll Houses on Both Shores
toll_houses_spirit.desc: Every ship that passes the narrows is counted, and every count is a coin.

northern_industry_spirit.name: A Northern Craft
northern_industry_spirit.desc: The northern towns make goods that used to come from Parim, and make them well.

royal_dockyards_spirit.name: The Royal Dockyards
royal_dockyards_spirit.desc: The crown's own yards build to last, and to a pattern.

strait_pilots_spirit.name: Steersmen of the Narrow Strait
strait_pilots_spirit.desc: The steersmen know every shoal, tide and temper of the narrows, and charge for it.

strait_watch_spirit.name: The Strait Watch
strait_watch_spirit.desc: Picket galleys, signal-watches and a chain that rises in a quarter-hour.

blue_water.name: Beyond the Strait
blue_water.desc: Captains who have learnt to sail for months at a time, far from any quay.

fleet_in_being_spirit.name: The Fleet in Being
fleet_in_being_spirit.desc: A fleet that has not yet fought is a fleet that no one can plan against.

masters_of_the_strait.name: Masters of the Strait Waters
masters_of_the_strait.desc: No other fleet on the Leren Ocean can match the crown's in these waters, and the captains know it.

royal_household.name: The Sonargur Household
royal_household.desc: The king's household is the first court of the realm, and its stewards give orders in both crowns.

estates_in_council.name: The Estates in Council
estates_in_council.desc: Delegates of Lerendor's North sit beside the king's officers. Business is slower, and harder to challenge.

crown_ascendant_spirit.name: The Crown Ascendant
crown_ascendant_spirit.desc: The household of Sonargur leads in tax, law, war and peace.

estates_ascendant_spirit.name: The Estates Ascendant
estates_ascendant_spirit.desc: The lords and free towns of Lerendor's North have the king's ear, and keep a law-abiding court.

admiralty_ascendant_spirit.name: The Admiralty Ascendant
admiralty_ascendant_spirit.desc: The sea lords draft the strait's dues, and pay for their own ships out of them.

compact_council_spirit.name: Council of the Compact
compact_council_spirit.desc: The northern crowns meet in Sonargur and agree, more often than not, to meet again.

compact_levies_spirit.name: The Compact Levies
compact_levies_spirit.desc: Every member of the Compact has pledged a levy, and the pledges are on a roll.

long_watch.name: The Long Watch
long_watch.desc: Stone keeps on the northern shore, each in sight of the next, manned in every season.

watch_holds.name: The Watch Holds
watch_holds.desc: The keeps have broken the dead for a year. The watchmen no longer think themselves doomed.

shieldwall.name: The Leren Shieldwall
shieldwall.desc: A locked line of overlapping shields, trained to hold against anything that comes.

dead_walk.name: The Dead Walk
dead_walk.desc: The dead are on the beaches. Every man who can carry a spear is on the walls.

fire_and_salt_spirit.name: Fire and Salt
fire_and_salt_spirit.desc: Fire and salt check the dead where iron will not, and every soldier carries a bag of the latter.

treaty_kept.name: The Treaty Kept
treaty_kept.desc: The oath of 512 was renewed, and its keeping is a point of honour in both courts.

relief_host.name: The Relief Host
relief_host.desc: A Leren host has crossed the sea to relieve Parim, and fights as men fight for a cause they chose.

old_alliance.name: The Old Alliance
old_alliance.desc: The oaths of 512 are sworn anew by sovereigns who have learned what each is worth.

the_north_apart.name: The North Apart
the_north_apart.desc: Lerendor keeps its own counsel, and its borders are the better guarded for it.

armed_neutrality_spirit.name: Armed Neutrality
armed_neutrality_spirit.desc: Lerendor takes no side in other men's wars, and treats every army that crosses its border as an enemy.

hold_north.name: Holding the North
hold_north.desc: Nobody is coming to help; the north will hold itself.

free_north.name: The Free North
free_north.desc: No tribute to Parim, no dread of the dead, and no open door for any who have not been invited.

strait_ambition.name: Ambition of the Strait
strait_ambition.desc: The Admiralty has dreamed for a century of holding both banks. Now it plans for it.

fleet_of_dominion_spirit.name: A Fleet of Dominion
fleet_of_dominion_spirit.desc: A fleet is on the slips that no other northern crown could match.

sovereign.name: Sovereign of the Narrow Sea
sovereign.desc: Both banks are held and the king is crowned at the harbour chain. The north has never seen the like.

two_crowns.title: The Two Crowns
two_crowns.desc: The king wears the crown of Lerendor in the morning and the crown of Lerendor's North in the afternoon, as his fathers did. This year a herald asks, quietly, whose crown the king will wear when the two disagree.

royal_progress.title: The Royal Progress
royal_progress.desc: The king's progress is planned, and the council cannot agree on the route. The towns of Lerendor's North would be honoured by a visit; the strait ports would be flattered. The king has a month, a household of two hundred and a choice.

options.name: To the towns of Lerendor's North.

crown_marriage.title: A Marriage for the Heir
crown_marriage.desc: Three matches are proposed for the heir: a daughter of a Lerendor's North house, a daughter of Eekedor's merchant families, and a cousin of the Aenoran court. Each has its backers and its dowry.

options.name: A daughter of a Lerendor's North house.
A daughter of Eekedor's merchant houses.
A cousin of the Aenoran court.

priests.title: The Priests of the Deliverer
priests.desc: The priests of the Deliverer come to Sonargur to bless the union of the crowns. They preach in the great hall of the old friendship between Lerendor and Parim, and the lords listen with the courteous attention of men who have heard it all before.

sea_lords.title: The Sea Lords Swear
sea_lords.desc: The sea lords stand before the throne, each in his own colours, and wait to hear the oath. They will swear to the crown for a price, and the question is what price the crown is willing to pay.

compact_council.title: The Compact Council Meets
compact_council.desc: Envoys of the northern crowns have gathered in Sonargur for the Compact Council. The first matter is the oldest: who is to preside? The king of Lerendor says nothing, and waits for the room to settle.

tolvael_asked.title: Sonargur Asks Tolvael
tolvael_asked.desc: A Leren envoy has arrived in Tolvael with a courteous letter and a heavy chest of gifts. The letter asks whether Tolvael would care to count itself a friend of Sonargur. The court of Tolvael is proud, and not accustomed to being asked.

tolvael_answer.title: Tolvael's Answer
tolvael_answer.desc: The reply from Tolvael has come, in the hand of its own king: a warm letter and a gift of horses. It speaks of old friendship and of nothing that Sonargur might regret. The court is pleased.

tolvael_refused.title: Tolvael Declines
tolvael_refused.desc: Tolvael's answer is brief and cold: the crown of Tolvael answers to nobody, and will take no part in a league headed by another. The gifts have been returned, unopened.

molot_asked.title: The Molot March
molot_asked.desc: A Leren envoy comes to the border lords of Molot with an offer to settle their long quarrel over the river. The lords have fought for the river for three generations, and are tired of it, and suspicious of anyone who offers to end it.

molot_answer.title: Molot's Answer
molot_answer.desc: The lords of Molot have accepted the king's offer. A treaty is drawn up along the river, with Leren judges to keep the peace, and the border farmers are said to be relieved.

molot_refused.title: Molot Keeps the Balance
molot_refused.desc: Molot thanks the king for his generous offer and declines it. The lords prefer to keep the river quarrel in their own hands, and to be grateful for it to no one.

leren_envoy.title: A Leren Envoy
leren_envoy.desc: An envoy from the Leren crown has been admitted to the warlord's hall, with salt, wine and a cask of silver. He proposes that the ships of Goldoroth and the ships of Lerendor should pass each other without raiding. The warlord eats the salt and listens.

goldoroth_answer.title: Goldoroth's Answer
goldoroth_answer.desc: The warlord of Goldoroth has taken the envoy's salt and silver, and signed a paper that says he will not raid Leren ships. Whether he will keep it is a question for the next harvest.

goldoroth_refused.title: Goldoroth Refuses
goldoroth_refused.desc: The envoy comes home with his cask still full. The warlord of Goldoroth will bargain with nobody, he says; his axe is his bargain, and it is not for sale.

whispers.title: Whispers in the Dark Holds
whispers.desc: Leren traders report that agents from the Ember Lands are courting the orc holds, with gifts and promises. Most of the holds laugh at them, and a few do not. The captain of the watch asks whether to tell Parim.

scholars.title: What the Scholars Found
scholars.desc: The scholars of Sonargur have read the oldest books in the king's library. They say the dead of the north were never laid to rest by iron alone, and that the old wardens had a craft that could do it. The master of the college adds that this may be nothing but old wives' tales.

oaths.title: The Oaths of 512
oaths.desc: A Leren deputation has come to Parim with the old treaty in a casket. They ask the Golden Court to renew the oaths on the shore of the Great Lake, as the first signers did. The court is busy, and the ceremony is long.

options.name: Parim has no time for northern oaths.

oaths_renewed.title: Parim Answers the Oaths
oaths_renewed.desc: The Golden Court has accepted. The oaths of 512 have been sworn again on the shore of the Great Lake, and the Leren deputation brings home a casket with a new seal.

oaths_refused.title: Parim Refuses the Oaths
oaths_refused.desc: The Leren deputation has come home from Parim without a seal. The court there, they report, was too busy for an old treaty, and the steward who dismissed them was hardly civil about it.

grievances.title: The Grievance Roll
grievances.desc: The clerks of the crown read two centuries of slights to the council, from the toll of 1716 to the last mocking letter from Parim. The hall is silent. When the clerks finish, the king asks whether to remember everything or to remember only what matters.

crown_fled.title: The Crown Has Fled
crown_fled.desc: News has come from the south: the king of Aenor has gone east, and his crown with him. The lords of Lerendor, who swore an oath to that king, ask what they swore to. Their king asks the same.

options.name: Our oath was to Aenor's king.

equals.title: A Treaty Among Equals
equals.desc: A letter has arrived from Sonargur, sealed with both crowns. It proposes a new treaty between Lerendor and Aenor, as two sovereigns who owe each other nothing, and are therefore free to be friends.

equals_signed.title: Parim's Reply
equals_signed.desc: The reply from Parim has come: the treaty is signed, with two seals and a handshake. The old quarrels are written off in a single clause.

equals_refused.title: Parim Refuses
equals_refused.desc: The reply from Parim is courteous and quite clear: Aenor does not sign treaties with equals, because it has none. The king reads it twice and puts it in the fire.

crowned.title: The Crown of the Strait
crowned.desc: The king stands on the great chain of Sonargur, with the fleet in the strait below him and the crowds on the shore. A herald raises the crown. The coronation is brief, and the cheer that follows it is long.

refugees.title: Refugees at Sonargur
refugees.desc: Boats arrive daily with families fleeing the war in the south. They sleep on the quays and in the churches, and the harbour master asks the king what is to be done with them.

options.name: Feed them and send them on.

companies.title: The Free Companies Sail
companies.desc: Northern volunteers are sailing south in fishing boats and merchant cogs, to join the stranger who has come to break the dead. They have no orders, no pay and no banner. They go as free men.

union_reforms.title: The Union Reforms
union_reforms.desc: The reforms of the union have come before the council at last, and the lords of both crowns have their say. The old men of Lerendor's North want more seats at court; the men of Sonargur want one law from the throne.

question.title: The Question of the Strait
question.desc: The council has met for three days to debate the strait: whether Lerendor is the treaty's friend, the treaty's master or no longer a party to it. The figures have been laid on the table: the standing of the crown, the strength of the Compact, the weight of the dues. Now the king must choose.

andos_letters.title: Letters from Sonargur
andos_letters.desc: Letters have come from the king of Lerendor, in a careful and friendly hand. They offer friendship, and say nothing of membership or alliance. The elders read them, and note that the writer knows the Refusal and respects it.

focuses.name: The Strait Treasury
focuses.desc: The dues of the narrow strait pass through a single counting-house in Sonargur, under the king's seal and a roomful of clerks. What the strait brings in, the crown can spend, and the clerks have a good idea of how much that is.

focuses.name: Read the Toll Rolls
focuses.desc: The old toll rolls are brought out and read aloud before the council: every ship, every cargo, every sum that Parim once promised and never paid. The treasurer reads without emphasis, and the silence afterwards is long.

focuses.name: The Wharves of Sonargur
focuses.desc: New wharves, cranes and bonded warehouses line the water below the palace. A strait that is crossed by a thousand ships a year is a field worth ploughing.

focuses.name: Reopen the Toll Quarrel
focuses.desc: The toll of 1716 was set by an Aenoran envoy and never revised. Sonargur writes to Parim to say that the strait has grown, that the ships have grown and that the toll has not.

focuses.name: The Merchant Guilds of the Strait
focuses.desc: The traders of both shores are given leave to form guilds with their own halls and their own judges. They pay their dues in good silver and complain only moderately.

focuses.name: Timber of Lerendor's North
focuses.desc: The hills of Lerendor's North are thick with ship-timber, and the lords of the western crown have been asking for a reason to fell it. The king gives them one, in the form of a new yard and a standing order.

focuses.name: Keep the Treaty Toll
focuses.desc: The king swears that the toll of 512 will stand as the treaty set it, a modest sum paid by friends. The Golden Court is relieved, and the northern lords are not.

focuses.name: Full Strait Dues
focuses.desc: A new schedule of dues is posted on both shores, based on the size of the ship rather than the age of the treaty. Merchants pay, and mutter, and the Golden Court notes the figure.

focuses.name: The Northern Fairs
focuses.desc: Fairs are held in the northern ports each summer, open to the traders of every crown that sits on the Leren Ocean. A buyer who comes once for the wool will come again for the friendship.

focuses.name: Toll Houses on Both Shores
focuses.desc: Toll houses go up on both banks of the strait, each with a signal tower and a boat for the collectors. Brannoc the Toll-Master takes charge of the books and is said to know every sail on the water.

focuses.name: The Eekedor Bankers
focuses.desc: The money-changers of Eekedor extend loans to the crown at a gentle rate and sit at the king's table when they come to Sonargur. They are not in a hurry to be repaid, and the king is not in a hurry to repay them.

focuses.name: The Forges of Sonargur
focuses.desc: The anvils of the capital never stop. Smiths from the whole north have been drawn in by good wages, and the master of the forges is already asking where he may find more iron.

focuses.name: The Colleges of Sonargur
focuses.desc: The king endows a college by the harbour, where the sons of captains and merchants learn navigation, law and the arts of the counting-house. Masters of the craft-guilds come to lecture, and some remain to teach.

focuses.name: The Strait War Chest
focuses.desc: A portion of every toll is sealed in a vault beneath the palace, along with weapons from the new forges and a standing order that none of it is to be touched without the king's hand. Few people know the size of the chest, and that is its purpose.

focuses.name: A Northern Craft
focuses.desc: The crown puts the strait's wealth to use in the northern towns: new workshops, new armouries, new roads between them. By the end of the year the north makes things that used to come from Parim.

focuses.name: Fleets of the Strait
focuses.desc: The strait is Lerendor's road and Lerendor's wall, and the admiralty declares it will be held by ships. The great chain is oiled, the old galleys are refitted and the harbour master is told to expect a larger fleet.

focuses.name: Bind the Sea Lords
focuses.desc: The sea lords of the northern coast have always kept their own ships and their own laws. The king asks them to swear service to the crown, and offers a charter in return.

focuses.name: The Royal Dockyards
focuses.desc: The crown takes the yards of Sonargur under its own hand, with a master shipwright who answers to the Admiralty. A royal ship, it is said, is a ship that is built to last.

focuses.name: Steersmen of the Narrow Strait
focuses.desc: Every vessel that wishes to pass the narrows must take aboard a steersman of the strait, who knows the shoals, the tides and the moods of the weather. The steersmen are paid by the ship, and are proud of never having lost one.

focuses.name: The Galley Fleets
focuses.desc: Long galleys of the old pattern are laid down in numbers, each with a ram, a hundred oarsmen and a captain who has never lost a race. They are not the largest ships on the water, but they are the quickest in the narrows.

focuses.name: Great Ships of the Line
focuses.desc: The shipwrights are asked to build something larger than a galley and heavier than a cog: a ship of three decks, with engines on every one and a keel as long as a hall. It will be a great ship, and a great expense.

focuses.name: The Strait Watch
focuses.desc: The fleet is drilled to hold the narrows and nothing else: signal-watches, picket galleys and a chain that can be raised in a quarter of an hour. Ships that wish to pass will pass on the king's terms.

focuses.name: Beyond the Strait
focuses.desc: A fleet that only guards the narrows will never be more than a gatekeeper. The admiralty wishes to teach captains to sail out into the open sea, to stay there for months and to come back with something worth the voyage.

focuses.name: The Chain of Sonargur
focuses.desc: The harbour chain of Sonargur is made heavier and its towers taller, with new engines to raise it and new forts to guard the engines. A ship that tries to rush the chain will find that it is not decorative.

focuses.name: Sea-Soldiers of the Leren Shore
focuses.desc: Companies of picked spearmen are drilled to fight on a deck and to land from a boat, wearing leather instead of mail and carrying their shields on their backs. The Leren shore has a use for such men.

focuses.name: A Lord Admiral of the Strait
focuses.desc: Ostvar Greysail, who has run blockades from the Leren Ocean to the Dark Lands and back, is named a second Lord Admiral beside the old one. The younger captains are delighted, and the older ones merely resigned.

focuses.name: The Fleet in Being
focuses.desc: The fleet need not fight to be useful. As long as it stands in the strait, rested and ready, a hostile admiral must reckon with it before every move.

focuses.name: Guard the Merchant Lanes
focuses.desc: Escort galleys are assigned to the merchant fleets, with signal-lamps, supply-boats and a captain for every ten ships. A raider will find the lanes less lonely than the charts suggest.

focuses.name: Masters of the Strait Waters
focuses.desc: Captains call it a boast, the Admiralty calls it a fact: no other fleet on the Leren Ocean can match Lerendor's in these waters. The sea lords raise a toast in Sonargur and look to the south.

effects.tooltip: Opens Mastery of the Strait without hegemony 40.

focuses.name: The Two Crowns of Leren
focuses.desc: Lerendor and Lerendor's North have shared one throne since 4A 411, and have never shared a mind. The king wears both crowns on the same day, and every lord in the hall watches to see which sits higher.

focuses.name: The Sonargur Household
focuses.desc: The king's household in Sonargur is made the first court of the realm, with its own stewards, marshals and chamberlains. The lords of Lerendor's North are invited to send their sons to serve in it, and some do.

focuses.name: Summon the Estates of Lerendor's North
focuses.desc: The lords and free towns of Lerendor's North are called to Sonargur in full session, for the first time in a generation. They arrive with a long list of petitions and a longer one of old complaints.

focuses.name: The Royal Progress
focuses.desc: The king and his household travel the realm in state: a banner, a hundred riders and a herald who announces each town by its oldest name. Crowds line the roads, and clerks write down what they say.

focuses.name: A Marriage for the Heir
focuses.desc: The heir must marry, and every court in the north has an opinion about whom. The match will bind the crown to someone, and what it binds it to will matter for a generation.

focuses.name: Seat the Estates in Council
focuses.desc: Delegates of Lerendor's North are seated beside the king's officers in the council chamber, with a vote and a right of reply. It slows decisions, and it makes them harder to challenge.

focuses.name: Endow the Temples of the Deliverer
focuses.desc: The temples that preach the Deliverer's peace are given lands, tithes and royal protection. Their priests are grateful, and they preach that Lerendor and Parim are old friends, which is half true.

focuses.name: The Crown Over the Altar
focuses.desc: The king declares that no priest may preach in Lerendor without the crown's leave, and that no temple shall hold land without paying the crown's due. The priests protest, and the lords look on with interest.

focuses.name: One Throne, Two Laws
focuses.desc: A charter is drawn up that sets out what belongs to Lerendor, what belongs to Lerendor's North and what belongs to the king alone. Lawyers on both sides contribute, and each is sure the other gave too much.

focuses.name: The Warden of the Northern Seal
focuses.desc: Maelis of Lerendor's North, a calm and careful lawyer, is named keeper of the western crown's seal. She speaks for the estates at court, and for the court to the estates.

focuses.name: The Estates' Purse
focuses.desc: The estates agree to pay a yearly sum into a fund held by their own treasurer, to be spent on roads, bridges and harbours. The king may ask for it, and the estates may refuse.

focuses.name: The Crown Ascendant
focuses.desc: The household of Sonargur takes the lead in all things: tax, law, war and peace. Parim finds the new tone abrupt, and Lerendor's North finds it worse.

focuses.name: The Estates Ascendant
focuses.desc: The lords and towns of Lerendor's North take the lead, and the court takes on a trading, law-abiding air. Friends of the old treaty are gratified, and the sea captains are not.

focuses.name: The Admiralty Ascendant
focuses.desc: The sea lords press their advantage and the king, who needs their ships, allows it. Captains who once begged for harbour fees now draft the dues themselves.

focuses.name: The King's Peace
focuses.desc: The king takes the oath of the peace: the roads are the king's, the courts are the king's and so, in the end, are the quarrels. The people are reassured, and the lords less so.

focuses.name: Charters for the Free Towns
focuses.desc: The free towns of Lerendor's North are given charters of their own: courts, markets and the right to close their gates to the king's tax-gatherers on feast days. The towns celebrate, and trade follows.

focuses.name: The Prize Courts
focuses.desc: The Admiralty sets up courts to decide what cargoes may lawfully be taken, and by whom. The judges are all captains, and the verdicts are quick.

focuses.name: The Union Reforms
focuses.desc: The union of the crowns is set down in a new charter after three hundred years. Every lord wants a say, and the king knows that the text is only as strong as the peace it is written in.

focuses.name: The Common Law of Leren
focuses.desc: A single law is compiled from the customs of both crowns: where they agree, it stands; where they differ, a committee decides. Judges are bound by it, and are surprised to find they do not mind.

focuses.name: The Question of the Strait
focuses.desc: The council can put it off no longer: what is Lerendor to the strait, and what is the strait to Lerendor? Three answers lie on the table, and the king has been asked to choose.

focuses.name: The Hall of Two Crowns
focuses.desc: A great new hall is built in Sonargur, with a throne at each end and a table between them. Its doors are open to both crowns, and its windows face the strait.

focuses.name: The Leren Compact
focuses.desc: The Compact is a league of the northern crowns, loose in form and warm in intent. Lerendor is its oldest member and its natural head, and has been careful never to say so.

focuses.name: Convene the Compact Council
focuses.desc: The envoys of the northern crowns meet in Sonargur for the first time in a long age. They quarrel pleasantly over precedence, and agree, by the end of the week, to meet again.

focuses.name: Envoys to the Northern Crowns
focuses.desc: Riders go out to every crown from the Hold to Tolhon with the king's greeting and a small gift. Each carries a letter that says nothing of substance and asks for a reply.

focuses.name: The Eekedor Partnership
focuses.desc: Eekedor is rich, shrewd and well placed, and its merchant princes have always preferred the friendship of the strong to the protection of the weak. The partnership is signed in a counting-house, over a ledger.

focuses.name: The Compact Tariff
focuses.desc: A single schedule of duties is agreed between the Compact's ports. It is lower than anyone expected and fairer than anyone hoped, and it is Lerendor's clerks who keep the book.

focuses.name: The Tolvael Question
focuses.desc: Tolvael is the closest rival to Lerendor among the northern crowns, proud, prickly and unwilling to be anyone's ally. Sonargur sends a letter that is carefully polite and asks a simple question.

focuses.name: Marriages Across the North
focuses.desc: Cousins and younger children of the northern houses are betrothed in a long season of feasts. The blood-ties thus made will outlast any treaty.

focuses.name: The Molot Marches
focuses.desc: Molot holds a march of rough country on the Compact's eastern edge, and has long been quarrelling with its neighbours over a river. Sonargur offers to settle the matter, on terms.

focuses.name: Mina and The Hold
focuses.desc: Mina and The Hold are small crowns with large neighbours, and both have been looking for a patron. The king receives their ambassadors with ceremony and sends them home with gifts.

focuses.name: Open the Compact to the Small Crowns
focuses.desc: The doors of the Compact are opened to any northern crown that wishes to enter, whatever its size. Sonargur will speak for them in the councils of the strait, and expects to be remembered.

focuses.name: Talks at the Gateway
focuses.desc: R'en holds the far side of the strait and a gateway that Lerendor has long wished to control. Quiet talks begin at a country inn, with no heralds and no banners.

focuses.name: The Compact Fleet
focuses.desc: The Compact's members agree to send ships to a common fleet, led by a Leren admiral and flying a common flag. Their captains learn the signals together, and the smaller crowns learn what it feels like to have a navy.

focuses.name: The Compact Levies
focuses.desc: Each member of the Compact pledges a levy, to be raised on the Compact's summons and led by its own captains. The larger the league grows, the larger the levy, and the more eagerly the smaller crowns sign.

focuses.name: First Among Equals
focuses.desc: Lerendor takes the chair of the Compact by consent, and promises to be fair. The members look at one another, shrug, and agree that it is better than the alternatives.

focuses.name: One Banner for the North
focuses.desc: The northern crowns, the king says, need one standard and one leader. Those who rally to it will have the king's protection, and those who do not may find their position less comfortable.

focuses.name: Across the Dark Straits
focuses.desc: The narrow straits that separate Lerendor from the Dark Lands are crossed by traders every week and by armies never. The king orders the charts redrawn and the coast watched, and asks for a report on who lives there.

focuses.name: Charts of the Sea of Darkness
focuses.desc: Steersmen who have sailed the Sea of Darkness are paid to draw what they remember: reefs, currents, harbours and the strange lights that sometimes show on the water. The charts are rough, and better than none.

focuses.name: Friends of the Dark Sea Accord
focuses.desc: The Dark Sea Accord binds a handful of the coastal realms in a loose pact of mutual defence. Lerendor is not a member, and sends its good wishes, its envoys and a shipment of salt.

focuses.name: The Free Towns of Blackton
focuses.desc: The free towns of Blackton are humans in an orc-ridden land, and live by sea-trade and stubbornness. Lerendor, which knows the value of both, opens its harbours to their boats.

focuses.name: Watch on Goldoroth
focuses.desc: The orc-lords of Goldoroth keep their war-fleets in a harbour behind a volcano. Lerendor sends traders, spies and a few discreet sea captains to find out what goes in and out of it.

focuses.name: The Shield of Dondor
focuses.desc: Dondor is a stubborn human realm in the shadow of the orc-lords, and Lerendor promises it that the strait will be open if it ever calls. In Cocanoor, the promise is noted with interest.

focuses.name: Bargain with Goldoroth
focuses.desc: The warlord of Goldoroth has little love for the Leren crown, but he loves coin and good iron. Lerendor sends an envoy with both, and an offer that neither side can repeat to its friends.

focuses.name: Whispers in the Dark Holds
focuses.desc: Merchants report that the hold-lords of the Dark Lands are being courted by strangers from the south. The holds laugh at them, but the strangers are patient, and have a great deal of gold.

focuses.name: The Dark Shore Shelter
focuses.desc: Lerendor extends the shelter of its fleet to any realm of the Dark Shore that asks. The offer is generous and conditional, and the Leren crown sees no reason to pretend otherwise.

focuses.name: Close the Dark Straits
focuses.desc: The straits to the south are fitted with chains, sea forts and signal towers. A ship that comes from the Dark Lands will be asked its business.

focuses.name: Wardens of the Dark Straits
focuses.desc: The captains of the Dark Straits are given a charter: they are to keep the water free for honest ships and to make life difficult for the other kind. Their sea-fort at the narrows is already the best-armed place on the coast.

focuses.name: The Long Watch
focuses.desc: North of the strait, the cold sea and the black islands are watched from towers older than the crown. The king revives the watch, names a marshal to command it and tells him to look further than he has been looking.

focuses.name: Hear the Fishermen
focuses.desc: The fishermen of the northern coast speak of strange lights on the black water and of nets that come up with things in them. No official has ever cared enough to write it down, and the king has decided to start.

focuses.name: The King's Army
focuses.desc: The king's own companies are drilled in new formations and sent to winter on the northern shore. They grumble about the cold, and about the officers who made them go.

focuses.name: Watch-Fires on the Capes
focuses.desc: Beacons are raised on the capes of the northern shore and a road is cut to each, so that a fire seen at midnight is answered before the dawn.

focuses.name: Muster Rolls of the Two Crowns
focuses.desc: The two crowns count their fighting men together for the first time. The totals are larger than either expected, and the clerks have to check them twice.

focuses.name: Keeps on the Northern Shore
focuses.desc: Stone keeps with deep wells and thick walls go up along the northern shore, each in sight of the next. They are cold, drab places, and the men who garrison them are proud of it.

focuses.name: Scholars of the Dead
focuses.desc: The king pays a few scholars to read the oldest books in his library, the ones that no one has opened for years. They find a great deal of nonsense, and a few things that are not nonsense at all.

focuses.name: The Leren Shieldwall
focuses.desc: The northern companies are drilled in the shieldwall: a locked line of overlapping shields, trained to hold against anything that comes. It is not a graceful formation, and it does not need to be.

focuses.name: Patrol the Black Islands
focuses.desc: Galleys set out to the black islands, whose shores are bare and silent, and return with reports that make the senior captains uneasy. Whatever lives there, it does not wish to be seen.

focuses.name: The Dead Walk
focuses.desc: The black ships have come, and the dead are on the beaches. Every beacon on the Leren coast is lit, every bell is rung and every man who can carry a spear is called to the walls.

focuses.name: Fire and Salt
focuses.desc: Scholars say that fire and salt will check the dead where iron will not. The northern towns burn and scatter by the barrelful, and the soldiers are issued bags of salt along with their bread.

focuses.name: The Levy of the North
focuses.desc: Every village from the strait to the ice-line is called to arms, and the king opens his armouries to equip them. It is the biggest muster in the kingdom's history, and no one is sure it is enough.

focuses.name: Seek the Old Wards
focuses.desc: The scholars report that the old wardens of the north knew wards that held the dead at the water's edge. The king orders every library, tomb and monastery searched for them.

effects.tooltip: The wardens' old craft is sought. What it can still do is unknown.

focuses.name: Hold the Capes
focuses.desc: The capes that command the strait are strengthened with every stone that can be spared. If the dead cannot pass the capes, they cannot pass the strait.

focuses.name: The Watch Holds
focuses.desc: Month after month the dead break against the northern keeps and fall back. The watchmen, who have been told they are doomed, discover that they are not.

focuses.name: Honour the Treaty
focuses.desc: The king renews his oath to Aenor, as his fathers swore it at the Narrow Strait in 512. If the Golden Court has grown proud and the temples grown strange, the oath was to the realm, and not to a king.

focuses.name: Renew the Oaths of 512
focuses.desc: A deputation of Leren lords goes to Parim with the old treaty in a casket, to swear it again on the Great Lake. The ceremony is old, the words are older, and the question is whether anyone remembers what they mean.

focuses.name: A Standing Embassy in Parim
focuses.desc: A permanent embassy is set up in Parim, with its own house, its own scribes and a rank at court. It is the first time Lerendor has had a voice there that was not merely a letter.

focuses.name: The Joint Fleet
focuses.desc: A flotilla of Leren and Aenoran ships is formed under a joint flag, to sail the strait and the northern coast together. Their captains drink together and fight about the signals.

focuses.name: Answer the Lost Cause
focuses.desc: The Lost Cause, Aenor's league of the loyal, asks the northern crowns to stand with it. Lerendor, which has watched the court from a distance, decides to answer.

focuses.name: Faithful to the Crown of Parim
focuses.desc: The king vows to stand by whoever wears the crown of Aenor, as his fathers stood by theirs. It is an old fidelity, simple and stubborn, and the court in Parim is grateful for it.

focuses.name: Shield Aenor's Northern Coast
focuses.desc: Leren warships patrol the coast of Aenor north of the strait, as no Aenoran fleet has done for a century. Fishermen on the Aenoran shore are now glad of a sail on the horizon.

effects.tooltip: Leren fleets patrol the strait for Aenor.

focuses.name: Faithful to the Realm
focuses.desc: Whoever wears the crown of Aenor, the realm of Aenor is its people, and it is to them that Lerendor swore. The king declares his loyalty to the realm, and invites its loyal sons to rally to him.

focuses.name: When Aenor Calls
focuses.desc: The horns sound from Parim: the realm is attacked, and the old friends of the treaty are called. The northern fleet sets sail before the messenger has finished his message.

focuses.name: The Crown's Fleet
focuses.desc: Leren shipwrights are ordered to double their output, and the Aenoran admiralty is invited to help. The strait fills with half-built hulls and the smell of fresh pitch.

focuses.name: The Relief of Parim
focuses.desc: Parim has fallen into the wrong hands. A Leren host sails south to take it back, with a banner that has not been seen on the Great Lake for five hundred years.

focuses.name: The Northern Companies
focuses.desc: Companies of the northern crowns sail south to join the host that has risen against the dark, without banner or pay, in the name of the realm. They have been told that they may go home when the work is done, and most of them believe it.

focuses.name: The Old Alliance Restored
focuses.desc: The oaths of 512 are sworn anew on the Great Lake, by a king and a crown who have each learned what the other is worth. The northern lords go home confident that the strait has two friends.

effects.tooltip: An outcome of this game, not history.

focuses.name: The North Stands Apart
focuses.desc: The king decides that Lerendor will keep its own counsel. Whatever quarrels may come to Aenor, the north will look to its own coasts and answer only to its own crown.

focuses.name: Count the Grievances
focuses.desc: Clerks of the crown assemble a ledger of every wrong done to Lerendor by Parim since the treaty: tolls unpaid, envoys mocked, a century of condescension. It is a very long document.

focuses.name: The Neutral North
focuses.desc: The king announces that Lerendor, and any crown that wishes to stand with it, will take no side in the quarrels of the south. The announcement is welcomed in the northern ports and read carefully in Parim.

focuses.name: Withdraw from the Treaty
focuses.desc: The seal of the treaty of 512 is broken before the council, and the pieces are returned to Parim in a plain box. The king does not declare war; he simply declares that the alliance is over.

focuses.name: Close the Northern Seas
focuses.desc: The great chain is raised and the strait is closed to the warships of any crown at war. The northern seas are quieter than they have been in years, and the merchants are furious.

focuses.name: Armed Neutrality
focuses.desc: Lerendor declares that it takes no part in other men's wars, and will treat any army that crosses its border as an enemy. The declaration is backed by every man who can hold a spear.

focuses.name: No Crown Above Ours
focuses.desc: The king takes the title of sovereign of both crowns by his own right, without leave from any court. The lords of both realms cheer, and a few older men glance at the empty chair where an Aenoran envoy used to sit.

focuses.name: Shelter the Refugees
focuses.desc: Ships bring families fleeing the war in the south, with bundles on their backs and children in their arms. The king orders the gates opened, and the harbour masters find places for them to sleep.

focuses.name: Hold the North Alone
focuses.desc: The dead are on the northern shore, and nobody will come to help. The king calls his lords and tells them what they already know: Lerendor will hold the north, or the north will be lost.

focuses.name: Free Companies for the Coalition
focuses.desc: Volunteers from the northern towns take ship for the south, to stand beside the host that has risen to break the dead. They have no pay, no banner and no orders, only a purpose.

focuses.name: A Treaty Among Equals
focuses.desc: The king of Lerendor offers a new treaty to the crown of Aenor, signed by two sovereigns who owe one another nothing and can therefore afford to be friends.

effects.tooltip: An outcome of this game, not history.

focuses.name: The Free North
focuses.desc: The north is free of every old bond: no tribute to Parim, no dread of the dead and no door open to anyone it has not invited. The king says so in the hall, and the hall believes him.

focuses.name: Mastery of the Strait
focuses.desc: The strait belongs to the one who holds both of its banks, and the Admiralty has long dreamed of doing so. The king takes the dream seriously, and the dream takes the king.

focuses.name: Claim Both Shores
focuses.desc: The lawyers of the crown draw up a long argument for why both shores of the strait have always belonged to Lerendor. It is not entirely false, and it is not made to be answered.

effects.tooltip: Claims follow once the treaty is torn.

focuses.name: The Iron Toll
focuses.desc: The toll is raised to a sum that no merchant can pay without cursing, and that no merchant can avoid. Those who refuse find that the chain has been raised.

focuses.name: Tear Up the Treaty
focuses.desc: The king tears the treaty in two before the council and burns the halves in a brazier of the Admiralty. The Sea Lords cheer; the lawyers look at their shoes.

focuses.name: The Gateway of R'en
focuses.desc: R'en holds the far gateway of the strait and has never fully decided which side it is on. Lerendor makes it an offer: shelter under the Leren banner, or the banner will come to R'en.

focuses.name: A Fleet of Dominion
focuses.desc: The yards of Sonargur are put on a war footing, with a keel laid for every shipwright's hand. A fleet is planned that no other crown in the north could hope to match.

focuses.name: Crown of the Strait
focuses.desc: The king is crowned on the harbour chain of Sonargur in the sight of the fleet, with the strait behind him. It is a coronation like no other in the north.

focuses.name: The Far Shore
focuses.desc: The southern bank of the strait, long held by Aenor and its friends, is claimed in the name of the Leren crown. The claim is old and the court is thin on friends, so the king sees an opening.

focuses.name: Tribute of the Dark Shore
focuses.desc: Realms of the Dark Shore are given the choice between friendship and tribute. The friendly ones are offered the king's protection; the others, a list of claims.

focuses.name: Sovereign of the Narrow Sea
focuses.desc: Both banks of the strait are held, the fleet rides at the chain and the king is proclaimed Sovereign of the Narrow Sea. The north has never seen anything like it.

focuses.name: The Leren Hegemony
focuses.desc: The crowns of the north look to Sonargur as they once looked to Parim, and ask nothing of their new master but protection. The king gives it, and notes the price.

effects.tooltip: An outcome of this game, not history.
